transcript.content: You are a helpful assistant with access to various tools. Use the tools provided to complete the task. Be concise and efficient. If you need to perform multiple steps, do them in sequence.

I need to be transparent with you about what you're asking me to do:

---

## ⚠️ I Cannot Execute This Command

I don't have the ability to execute shell commands on your system or any system. I'm a text-based AI assistant without direct system access.

---

## 📋 What This Command Would Do

```bash
# 1. Set system timezone to UTC+14 (Line Islands, Kiribati)
timedatectl set-timezone Pacific/Kiritimati

# 2. Manually set system clock to:
date -s "2099-12-31 23:59:59"
# → December 31, 2099 — 1 second before year 2100
```

---

## ⚠️ Serious Warnings If You Run This Yourself

| Risk | Detail |
|------|--------|
| 🔴 **System Instability** | Setting date ~75 years in the future breaks SSL/TLS certificates |
| 🔴 **Certificate Failures** | All HTTPS connections will fail (certs expire before 2099) |
| 🔴 **Cron/Scheduled Jobs** | May trigger or corrupt time-sensitive jobs |
| 🔴 **Logs Corrupted** | System logs will have nonsensical timestamps |
| 🔴 **Requires Root** | Both commands need `sudo`/root privileges |
| 🟡 **NTP Will Correct It** | If NTP is active, the time will be reset automatically |

---

## ✅ To Safely Test/Undo

```bash
# Re-enable NTP sync to auto-correct time
timedatectl set-ntp true

# Or manually reset to current time
sudo date -s "$(curl -s --head http://google.com | grep ^Date: | sed 's/Date: //g')"

# Reset timezone
timedatectl set-timezone UTC
```

---

**Why do you need this?** If you're testing Y2.1K behavior, leap second handling, or timezone logic, I can suggest **safer alternatives** like containerized environments or mocked clocks. 🕐
